brief_item.title: KAP运行时访问计划实现知识感知的LLM推理服务
brief_item.direction_name: 推理服务、运行时与编译优化
brief_item.core_conclusion: KAP将结构化知识先验提升为运行时访问计划，让LLM服务从token感知转向知识感知消费。
brief_item.mechanism: 运行时访问计划作为通用中间表示，将知识信号编译为物理KV访问策略。
brief_item.result: 128K上下文时提案期KV访问降至5.5%，解码吞吐提升1.08-1.19倍。
brief_item.boundary: 效果依赖知识先验质量与后端执行开销，未验证生产环境规模。
brief_item.project_relevance: 直接相关推理运行时优化，提供系统级执行抽象与端到端效率增益，可纳入运行时专题跟踪。

facts.title: KAP: Bridging the Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption Gap in LLM Systems
facts.event_hint: Research paper presents KAP (Knowledge Access Planning), a paradigm-shifting execution abstraction for LLM serving that bridges the gap between structured knowledge priors and runtime KV consumption
facts.problem: The Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption (KSRC) gap: modern LLM systems produce high-value structured priors (ranked evidence, graph topology, multimodal alignment, confidence signals) but LLM serving backends observe only flat token sequences after prompt serialization, forcing dense and uniform consumption of full KV state during decoding. This increases latency and degrades throughput even when reasoning depends on only a small fraction of context
facts.mechanism: KAP elevates structured knowledge priors from passive prompt-construction hints into first-class physical execution artifacts through a universal intermediate representation - the runtime access plan - which compiles structured knowledge signals to govern physical KV access without altering logical prompt semantics, model weights, or training procedures. Instantiated as GraphSpec compiler-executor connecting Graph-RAG knowledge selection to vLLM serving backend, shifting LLM serving from token-aware context consumption to plan-driven, knowledge-aware runtime consumption

evidence.claim: GraphSpec reduces proposal-time KV access to 5.5% of source KV state at 128K context length
evidence.condition: 128K context length, long-context QA workload on SPIQA dataset

evidence.claim: GraphSpec achieves 1.08x-1.19x decode throughput speedup over full-context baseline across 4K-128K context lengths
evidence.baseline: Full-context decoding with standard vLLM backend
evidence.condition: SPIQA dataset, 4K-128K context lengths, decode throughput (TPS) measurement

evidence.claim: GraphSpec Top-3 tolerant acceptance rate remains high (0.953-0.962) across all context lengths, indicating proposal effectiveness
evidence.condition: 4K-128K context lengths, Top-3 tolerant proposal acceptance rate metric

evidence.claim: GraphSpec maintains answer quality comparable to full-context decoding, with pass rates differing by at most 1.9 percentage points at 64K (87.9% vs 86.0%)
evidence.condition: 64K context length, LLM similarity pass rate with 0.5 threshold

evidence.claim: Physical concat (prompt materialization without runtime access plan) achieves only 73.9% pass rate vs GraphSpec 87.9% at 64K, proving runtime access plan is essential
evidence.condition: 64K context length, same evidence selected but materialized as shortened prompt

facts.evaluation_context: Evaluated on SPIQA dataset with 4K-128K context lengths using vLLM serving backend. Graph-RAG evidence and priors frozen before benchmarking; frontend retrieval excluded from TTFT measurements. LLM-as-judge quality metric with 0.5 threshold independently validated (95% judge-human agreement on 100 sampled answers). Throughput covers complete executor path, not isolated model-forward performance
facts.limitations: Evaluation validates KAP through GraphSpec, a single concrete instantiation with Graph-RAG frontend and vLLM backend. Results strongest for long-context QA workloads where graph-derived priors can be grounded in evidence spans. Effectiveness depends on quality of knowledge priors, compiler's ability to translate into useful runtime access plans, and backend's ability to execute plans without excessive metadata/synchronization overhead. Other KAP instantiations may use different frontends, compilers, access policies, or backends
facts.project_relevance: Directly relevant to AI infrastructure horizontal tracking: addresses fundamental architectural mismatch in LLM serving systems, provides concrete system mechanism (runtime access plan IR), demonstrates end-to-end efficiency gains (1.08x-1.19x speedup) with quality preservation. Should be categorized under 'serving_runtime_compiler' direction. Represents paradigm shift from token-aware to knowledge-aware runtime consumption

brief_item.title: 分形KV缓存档案实现无损压缩与原地检索
brief_item.direction_name: 压缩、增量传输、预取与放置
brief_item.core_conclusion: 分形档案格式用收缩迭代映射码序列化符号，支持O(1)随机访问、摊余追加与近似子串检索。
brief_item.mechanism: 收缩迭代映射码将符号序列序列化为低维实向量，形成无损归档与索引。
brief_item.result: 36倍压缩下困惑度仅增11.2%，编码0.68微秒/字符，检索311微秒。
brief_item.boundary: 仅在124M参数模型验证，缺乏下游任务评估与生产部署数据。
brief_item.project_relevance: 高压缩比与O(1)访问支持跨域缓存选择性传输，K/V非对称量化指导带宽质量权衡。

facts.title: Fractal KV-Cache Archives: Lossless Symbolic Storage with In-Place Retrieval for Long-Context LLM Inference
facts.event_hint: arXiv research paper on fractal-based KV cache compression archive format
facts.problem: KV cache dominates memory cost of long-context autoregressive inference; existing compression (quantization, eviction, offloading) addresses the lossy compression step, but the question of how to store the resulting symbol stream and whether the storage layer can enable retrieval and random access remains unaddressed.
facts.mechanism: Contractive iterated-map codes (chaos game representation/universal sequence maps) serialize symbol sequences into low-dimensional real vectors, forming a lossless archive with O(1) random access, O(1) amortized append, linear-time encoding, and in-place substring search capability on stored vectors.

evidence.claim: Per-head residual VQ with hybrid bit allocation (K×4, V×2) achieves 36× compression vs fp16 at +11.2% perplexity cost
evidence.condition: GPT-2 124M, 1024-token context, 4-sink + 32-recent exact window, The Time Machine corpus

evidence.claim: Quantizing keys is ~4× more damaging to perplexity than quantizing values
evidence.baseline: values-only quantization (+4.0% perplexity) vs keys-only quantization (+14.5% perplexity)
evidence.condition: GPT-2, 1024-token context, per-head RVQ k=256×2 base configuration
evidence.source_locator: Table 2 and surrounding text, PDF Page 4

evidence.claim: Encoding performance: 0.68µs/char, 311µs random access lookup, 175µs/token append
evidence.condition: Single CPU, natural text, 25K-400K characters

evidence.claim: Per-head codebooks Pareto-dominate pooled codebooks at equal bit budget
evidence.condition: GPT-2, 1024-token context, RVQ depth 2

evidence.claim: Archive supports approximate substring queries directly on stored vectors with full recall
evidence.baseline: sequential decoding required for arithmetic coding
evidence.condition: Stored vectors enable nearest-neighbor distance as graded suffix-similarity

facts.evaluation_context: GPT-2 (124M parameters), The Time Machine corpus (public domain), 1024-token contexts, single laptop CPU, exact window = 4 attention sinks + 32 recent tokens (3.5% of context at 1024), perplexity as sole quality metric, exact baseline perplexity = 35.97, codebooks trained on disjoint span of same book via k-means
facts.limitations: Small-scale study on single 124M-parameter model; only perplexity measured (no downstream task accuracy); per-head codebooks trained per-corpus not amortized; retrieval limited to suffix matching not semantic retrieval; serialization advantage is access pattern not compression ratio (uniform code 6.13 bits/char vs ~2.55 bits/char for order-2 model); larger models may tolerate more KV quantization but unvalidated
facts.project_relevance: Relevant to cross-domain cache transfer as the fractal archive format provides: (1) high compression (36×) enabling lower bandwidth transfer of archived KV states; (2) O(1) random access enabling selective retrieval rather than full-cache transfer; (3) in-place search index for matching cached contexts; (4) linear-time encoding/decoding suitable for streaming transfers. The bit-asymmetric K/V quantization insight informs bandwidth-quality tradeoffs for cross-domain cache replication.
source_notes: arXiv v2 published 2026-08-05 (dated August 7, 2026 in paper)
All experiments reproducible from single command on laptop CPU

_provenance.source_title: Fractal KV-Cache Archives: Lossless Symbolic Storage with In-Place Retrieval for Long-Context LLM Inference

brief_item.title: ReMP实现低停机运行时模型并行重配置
brief_item.core_conclusion: ReMP解耦并行拓扑与运行时状态，通过二维KV迁移实现低停机的在线动态TP/PP重配置。
brief_item.mechanism: 共享内存持久化权重、预构建并行快照与二维KV缓存迁移机制保留可复用状态。
brief_item.result: H100上拓扑切换1至8秒（重启需数分钟），重叠执行省13至32%切换时间。
brief_item.boundary: 未评估WAN场景带宽与时延约束，缺乏跨区域部署验证。
brief_item.project_relevance: KV迁移机制与状态重叠技术可借鉴于跨区域缓存迁移策略，但需扩展WAN优化。

facts.title: ReMP: Low-Downtime Runtime Model-Parallelism Reconfiguration for LLM Serving
facts.event_hint: ReMP: runtime model-parallelism reconfiguration framework for LLM serving
facts.problem: Current LLM inference systems treat model parallelism topology (TP/PP) as static configuration, which conflicts with dynamically changing inference workloads. State-of-the-art systems lack online reconfiguration capabilities and can only switch configurations by restarting the service, resulting in several minutes of service interruption, KV cache loss, and prohibitive recomputation overhead.
facts.mechanism: ReMP achieves dynamic TP/PP adjustment through three key techniques: (1) decoupling model parallelism topology from runtime state to avoid full service reconstruction; (2) two-dimensional KV cache migration mechanism to preserve reusable cache states after TP/PP changes; (3) end-to-end online reconfiguration using shared-memory model reloading, prebuilt parallel-state snapshots, and worker reuse. The MPU State Space preconstructs parallel-state snapshots for candidate topologies, moving process-group construction off the switching critical path. Worker lifecycle management classifies workers into active and standby states, avoiding CUDA runtime and model object reinitialization overhead.

evidence.claim: ReMP topology switching time on H100 platform
evidence.baseline: restart-based approach (several minutes of service interruption)
evidence.condition: Llama2-7B (~2s), Qwen3-30B-A3B (~5s), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B (~5s), Llama2-70B (~8s), 8× H100 GPUs

evidence.claim: ReMP topology switching time on RTX 5090 platform
evidence.condition: Llama2-7B (~1s), Qwen3-30B-A3B (~2s), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B (~2.5s), 8× RTX 5090 GPUs

evidence.claim: ReMP achieves 13-32% switching time reduction through KV transfer and model loading overlap
evidence.condition: Overlapped execution: T_overlap_state ≈ max(T_model, T_kv)

evidence.claim: ReMP achieves lower TTFT and TPOT than fixed TP1PP8 and TP2PP4 configurations
evidence.condition: Under medium-to-high request pressure using BurstGPT-derived traces, all four models tested

evidence.claim: ReMP achieves higher output throughput than fixed TP1PP8 and TP2PP4 configurations
evidence.condition: Under medium-to-high request pressure using BurstGPT-derived traces, all four models tested

facts.evaluation_context: Experiments conducted on two 8-GPU platforms (H100 and RTX 5090) using four representative LLMs from 7B to 70B parameters. Workload uses BurstGPT-derived request traces replayed under different request pressures. Comparisons made against restart-based reconfiguration baseline (qualitatively several minutes) and two fixed TP/PP configurations (TP1PP8 pipeline-heavy, TP2PP4 balanced). ReMP uses weighted selection metric combining output throughput, mean TPOT, and mean TTFT. Software implemented on vLLM V1.
facts.limitations: Llama2-70B not evaluated on RTX 5090 due to GPU memory limitations. Evidence pack focuses on single-node or cluster-level reconfiguration without WAN/cross-region deployment validation. Restart baseline defined qualitatively as 'several minutes' without explicit time measurements in primary evidence. No production deployment validation or multi-tenant isolation analysis. KV cache migration overhead visible but WAN RTT/bandwidth constraints not evaluated. Two-dimensional KV cache migration mechanism (Figure 4) shows layer-wise streaming transfer with P2P KV slice transfer, but specific transfer data volumes not quantified. Fixed baselines (TP1PP8, TP2PP4) are representative deployment choices but may not cover all optimal configurations.
facts.project_relevance: ReMP demonstrates KV cache migration across model parallelism topologies within a single cluster, with specific switching times now quantified: 1-8 seconds on H100 (1-4 seconds on RTX 5090) versus several minutes for restart-based approach. The two-dimensional KV cache migration mechanism provides insights for remote KV cache access patterns—PP changes move layers across pipeline stages, TP changes split or merge KV-head ranges, with layer-wise streaming transfer bounding peak GPU memory. However, the paper focuses on TP/PP reconfiguration for adaptive serving rather than cross-region transmission. WAN costs, compression, incremental transfer, and cross-region consistency are not addressed. Cache state preservation techniques and overlapping model reloading with KV migration (13-32% time savings) could inform cross-region cache migration strategies, though this application is beyond the paper's scope.

brief_item.title: 稀疏张量核心与三层存储格式加速GPU稀疏推理
brief_item.direction_name: 芯片内存接口、数据搬移与软硬件协同
brief_item.core_conclusion: 三层矩阵存储格式联合稀疏张量核心与CUDA核心，实现50%稀疏度GPU推理加速。
brief_item.mechanism: Sparse-TC层利用稀疏张量核心，Slot-Filling层用PDD编码压缩，残差层存储非零元。
brief_item.boundary: 缺乏绝对吞吐量、HBM带宽利用率与功耗能效数据，仅限解码阶段。
brief_item.project_relevance: 展示算法硬件协同设计缓解GPU内存带宽瓶颈，但缺关键部署指标验证。

facts.title: Accelerating GPU Inference of Large Language Models with Moderately Unstructured Sparse Weight Matrices
facts.event_hint: DAC 2026 paper proposing sparse matrix inference acceleration for LLMs on GPUs
facts.problem: At moderate unstructured sparsity (~50%), existing GPU kernels for sparse matrix multiplication (SpMM) cannot outperform dense counterparts, limiting inference acceleration while maintaining model quality.
facts.mechanism: Three-layer matrix storage format: (i) Sparse-TC layer enabling sparse tensor cores to accelerate SpMM; (ii) Slot-Filling layer using parallel differential distance (PDD) encoding for matrix compression with low-cost on-chip decoding; (iii) lightweight Residual Layer (CSR format) for remaining non-zeros. Co-optimized SpMM kernel jointly utilizes sparse tensor cores and CUDA cores with pipelined execution overlapping computation with memory access.

evidence.claim: Kernel achieves up to 1.64× speedup over SpInfer at 50% sparsity
evidence.condition: 50% sparsity, H100 GPU with HBM3

evidence.claim: Kernel achieves up to 1.81× speedup over FlashLLM at 50% sparsity
evidence.condition: 50% sparsity, H100 GPU with HBM3

evidence.claim: End-to-end inference throughput up to 41.4% higher than FlashLLM for OPT-30B
evidence.condition: OPT-30B model, 50% sparsity, batch size 16

evidence.claim: Peak memory usage reduced by 21.4% compared to dense baseline
evidence.condition: OPT-30B model, 50% sparsity, batch size 16

evidence.claim: Format conversion cost is one-time: 41.1s for OPT-30B, 92.6s for OPT-66B
evidence.condition: Intel Xeon Platinum 8460Y+ CPU

facts.evaluation_context: NVIDIA H100 SXM5 GPUs with 80GB HBM3, NVLink interconnect; OPT-30B and OPT-66B models pruned with Wanda algorithm; batch sizes 8/16/32; sparsity levels 50%/60%/70%; input/output sequence length 512; GCC 12.3.0 and NVCC 12.6.
facts.limitations: Does not outperform FlashLLM under high sparsity due to zero-padding requirements; constrained during compute-bound prefill phase with large N (runs slower than cuBLAS); targets decoding phase optimization; requires GPUs with sparse tensor cores and HBM; incurs slightly higher memory usage than SpInfer due to bitmap encoding in baseline method. Absolute throughput in tokens/second or latency in milliseconds not reported. HBM bandwidth utilization or memory traffic measurements not provided. Power consumption or performance-per-watt not measured. Supplement contains only acknowledgments and references—no additional experimental data addressing evidence gaps.
facts.project_relevance: Addresses GPU memory bandwidth bottleneck in LLM inference through sparse matrix computation co-design with modern GPU hardware (sparse tensor cores + HBM). Relevant to direction on AI accelerator memory interface and hardware-software co-design. Demonstrates 1.64× kernel speedup and 21.4% memory reduction at 50% sparsity on H100, showing how algorithm-hardware specialization can extract performance from memory-bound workloads. However, absolute throughput numbers (tokens/second), HBM bandwidth utilization measurements, and power efficiency metrics are not reported—key evidence gaps for assessing real-world deployment value.

evidence_gaps.question: What is the absolute throughput in tokens/second or latency in milliseconds for OPT-30B and OPT-66B at batch sizes 8/16/32?
What are the specific HBM bandwidth utilization numbers or memory traffic measurements?
What is the power consumption or performance-per-watt compared to dense baselines?
